summary.title: Digests for the book "Scalability Rules: 50 Principles for Scaling Web Sites"
summary.one_liner: A slide digest of Abbott and Fisher's Scalability Rules, covering principles such as avoiding overengineering, scaling out instead of up, splitting work along X/Y/Z axes, and choosing the right data store.
keywords: scale cube x y z axis
takeaways: Complexity is the enemy of scalability; keep designs simple and avoid overengineering.
Scale out horizontally by cloning services and splitting work, rather than relying on ever-bigger machines (scale up).
Use the X axis (cloning), Y axis (split by service or data noun/verb) and Z axis (split similar data such as by customer ID) to distribute load.
Design for about 20x capacity, implement for 3x, and deploy for about 1.5x (the D-I-D approach) to scale just in time.
Choose storage by data needs: relational databases for ACID relationships, other tools for other data, and tiered storage as data ages.
summary.summary: This is a slide deck digest of the book Scalability Rules by Martin Abbott and Michael Fisher, presented as numbered rules with a consistent structure: what the rule is, when to apply it, how to do it, and why. The rules are grouped into themes such as reducing the equation, distributing work, using the right tools, and caching. Examples include the D-I-D capacity approach, a comparison of single-site versus multi-site cost, and a table comparing file systems, NoSQL and RDBMS. The text is cut off partway through the firewall rule, so the later sections are not covered.
